title: How I Clean Up Years of SharePoint Sprawl
description:
Inactive SharePoint sites are more than clutter. They consume storage, preserve old permissions, and can feed outdated content into Copilot and other AI tools.

In this video, I show you how to find inactive SharePoint sites using SharePoint Advanced Management, build an automated Site Lifecycle Management policy, and decide what should happen when a site is no longer being used.

🚀 What You'll Learn:
How to identify inactive SharePoint sites
Why inactive sites create security and AI readiness problems
SharePoint Advanced Management licensing requirements
How to run a site lifecycle assessment
How to create an inactive site policy
How to notify site owners for certification
How to automatically move inactive sites to read-only or archive
How to prevent stale sites from appearing in Copilot and search with Restricted Content Discovery

💡 Why Watch?
Years of SharePoint projects can leave behind hundreds of sites nobody actively manages. Those sites may still contain sensitive data, stale permissions, and outdated documents that AI tools can surface.

Site Lifecycle Management gives IT teams and MSPs a repeatable way to find that sprawl, validate whether sites are still needed, and automate what happens next.

👍 Engage with Me:
If you found this video helpful, hit Like, subscribe, and share it with someone managing SharePoint or Microsoft Copilot.

I'd also love to hear from you. How are you handling inactive SharePoint sites today?

Check out my free Skool community for more content on Secure AI Enablement:
